source: Brisbane City Council, City Plan 2014 - Significant landscape tree overlay
endpoint: https://data.brisbane.qld.gov.au/api/explore/v2.1/catalog/datasets/cp14-significant-landscape-tree-overlay/records (filtered to ovl2_desc='Individual or group significant landscape tree site sub-category')
licence_proof: hub.arcgis.com/api/v3/datasets/bed1dde0fb624870a93cbe58c0b8e0b2_0 (the dataset's own ArcGIS Hub source, linked from Brisbane's open data portal) attribute 'licenseInfo' reads verbatim: "This material is licensed under a Creative Commons - Attribution 4.0 licence. No access or use limitations." Also cross-confirmed by data.gov.au's harvested metadata for the same dataset (package 'cp14-significant-landscape-tree-overlay'), license_title 'CC-BY-4.0'. Fetched 2026-08-15.
designation: Statutory overlay under Brisbane City Plan 2014 (map reference OM-019.1), sub-category 'Individual or group significant landscape tree site', one of four sub-categories on the overlay (the other three, Adjoining site / Landscape features / Vegetation protection order, were excluded from this file as they mark protection zones or adjoining land rather than a designated tree itself; see caveat)
scope: 558 polygon records (converted here to their centroid point, 'geo_point_2d' as supplied by the API) across the City of Brisbane local government area, covering the whole city rather than one cluster. This is the raw overlay only: NO species, common name, age, girth or significance-reason field exists anywhere in this feature class. It is purely a regulatory boundary saying 'a significant landscape tree (or group) sits here', not a fact sheet about the tree.
caveat: MUCH THINNER THAN A NORMAL REGISTER: no species/age/name means this alone does not clear the two-independent-sources bar for a tree's basic facts (species, age) even though it is itself one legitimate 'official register' source for the tree's EXISTENCE and its being a council-designated significant tree. A verify pass must find species/age from elsewhere (satellite/street-level imagery for a distinctive crown, a second source, or an on-the-ground description) before any of these can move past a lead. No land-ownership or access flag exists either; the overlay applies to both public and private land under Brisbane's planning scheme (a Vegetation Protection Order can sit over a private-garden tree), so hard rule 10 needs a per-candidate check (aerial imagery / street view for whether the point sits on identifiable public park or street land) before anything ships. Total overlay was 1,740 records across all four sub-categories; this file keeps only the 558 tagged 'Individual or group significant landscape tree site', the closest match to a genuine per-tree designation. The other 1,182 (Adjoining site 625, Vegetation protection order 423, Landscape features 134) were NOT imported and are a different kind of designation, not folded in here.
